verdicts.reason: HELD, and it is the strongest item in the packet. I opened both frames myself. Crop A (duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png, x40-760 y920-1080, 2x): green 20/20, blue 26/26, and a THIRD bar that is an EMPTY brown track carrying pale-grey text 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE', yellow '150% DAMAGE' beneath. Crop B (duel_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t435.0s.png, same crop, same fighter, same buff, 7 s later): green 19/20, blue 26/26, and that same third bar is now roughly 40% filled solid WHITE with NO text on it whatsoever. The bar fills; the words go away. Every code line resolves verbatim: :328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);', :336 'if(_loc3_ == 0)' -> :340 sets htmlText to the grey label, :344 'else if(_loc3_ > 0 && _loc3_ < 1 && this.§1t5169s0§.visible)' -> :346 hides it, :348 'else if(_loc3_ >= 1)' plays Snd_criticalDamage and swaps in the black label, and :111 builds that grey label from getString(960) at colour #BBBBBB. strings.json has no '960' (2,533 keys checked in python), so it is web-only, exactly as claimed; ['175'] is 'Critical Hit'. I then closed the loop the finding did not: §1t99s0§.as:3325 shows the reload regen pushing (reload, maxreload) straight into that very HUD function §1t5205s0§, and android BattleUI.as:259-262 is the plain-named twin 'updateReload(percentage)' whose crittext is visible at percentage >= 1. So the third bar IS the reload/Focus meter, code-confirmed and frame-confirmed. RR:158 'In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717' falls, and so does RR:159-160's 'the in-combat switch is a recreation divergence': §1t99s0§.as:3058-3081 is a live in-combat stance CYCLER that early-returns only 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)'. THE FRAME WINS OVER THE MEASUREMENT DOC HERE, and I say so out loud: RR:178's own LOOK verdict read a transient low-Focus readout as a permanent lock. One correction to carry: the finding says the label shows 'exactly while reload <= 48' — true — but at reload == 48 exactly the label is still up while the cycler is already unlocked (>= 48), a one-tick overlap. Does not touch the overturn.

HELD. Every cited line resolves verbatim. §1t99s0§.as:3272 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' -> :3274 'return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;' is the return path of the stance damage roll §1t4475s0§ (:3255). §1t5957s0§.as:2727 / :2736 / :2745 each read '_loc42_ = 1.3;' in the Light / Balanced / Heavy branch of the stats-panel readout, applied at :2751-2752 as '_loc43_ = _loc1_ * _loc42_ + _loc12_'. :2746 '_loc47_ = 0.8;' is set ONLY inside the Heavy branch. I also opened the defence side the finding did not cite: §1t99s0§.as:3284-3288 is 'internal function §1t4477s0§() : int { if(this.stance == §1t12222s0§) { return defense * 0.8; }' — the one-way Heavy-defender penalty, in code, in the target build. RR:74's 'Critical = 1.3 x Physical; Heavy defender Defense x0.8 (one way)' is now web-source-backed rather than wiki-backed, RR:153-154's open ask '(Read a real OG crit popup to fully seal it.)' is discharged, and RR:190 blocker (2) 'crit 1.3 vs 3 final — read one crit popup' closes. The finding's self-imposed limit is honest but too modest, and I am NOT refuting it for that: it says ':3272 tests an equality between two obfuscated members, not a probability', which is exactly right, and the android twin de-obfuscates it — MCSPlayer.as:3215 'if(this.reload == this.maxreload)'. See my new finding CRIT-PROC. One real hazard the finding does not flag and a porter must: the android build's crit is NOT 1.3 (MCSPlayer.as:3219 '* 1.2', :3221 '* 1.5'), so 1.3 is web-only — filed separately.

HELD ON ITS HEADLINE, WITH TWO CORRECTIONS THE REWRITE MUST CARRY. The mechanic is real and I verified it in BOTH builds. §1t1523s0§.as:2346 reads verbatim 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5;' inside §1t9593s0§ (:2344), whose next line is 'return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));'; :254 is 'internal static const §1t9426s0§:int = 25;' and android StatsManager.as:220 is 'internal static var STAT_DAN:int = 25;'. The android twin names the function outright — StatsManager.as:1915 'internal static function getBaseSlashLengthVal(speed:int) : int', :1917 'var maxincrement:int = 90 + getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) * 5;' — so this IS the blade path, and MCSPlayer.as:3094 feeds the result to 'InputManager.setMaxDistance(this.slashLength)'. The arithmetic is right too: asymptote 120 + 90 = 210 at dan 0, 120 + 135 = 255 at dan 9. CORRECTION 1 (mis-cite): the ledger sentence it quotes, 'Dan-rank count/titles (garbled source)', is rebirth-elements blocker (3) at REBUILD_READINESS.md:205 — NOT :245. RR:245 is meta-social, whose blocker (3) is 'achievements list, daily-reward table, token costs', and nothing here touches it. The rewrite must land on :205. CORRECTION 2 (wrong ids, and it is the exact instruction the finding gives): 'must cite ids 455-464, not 456-464' is BACKWARDS. Both builds display 456-464 and never touch 455 — §1t5957s0§.as:3067-3102 and android InventoryUI.as:2274-2315 switch on STAT_DAN and emit '' for dan 0, then getString(456)..getString(464) for dan 1..9; grep for getString(455) returns zero hits in either build. There are TEN dan states (0-9, capped by StatsManager.as:2209 'if(getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) < 9)' -> :2211 'changeStat(STAT_DAN,1);') but NINE displayed titles. I hold the finding because the overturn it names — dan is mechanical, not cosmetic — survives both errors intact, and refuting would destroy a first-hand-verified mechanic. Minor: '+5 px' is +5 to the BASE, which then runs through the per-stance multipliers (MCSPlayer.as:3030 Light x1.5, :3041 Balanced, :3052 Heavy with a floor of 100), so Light actually gains ~7.5 per dan.

HELD, cleanly. §1t401s0§.as:1954 'var _loc3_:int = §1t1525s0§.§1t9936s0§();' then :1955-1958 clamp '_loc3_ > 80 -> 80', then :1959 'param1 = _loc3_ * 100;' — all verbatim. The three material tiers are exactly where claimed: :1968 'if(_loc3_ < 30)' with :1970 checking item 20061 < 2 and :1978 spending (20061,-2); :1980 'else if(_loc3_ < 60)' spending 20062 x1 + 20063 x2; :1993 'else' spending 20061 x2 + 20060 x2 + 20065 x1. resolved_names.json gives 20060 Coal, 20061 Iron Ore, 20062 Tin Ore, 20063 Copper Ore, 20065 Titanium Ore, and strings 845/846/847 read 'Materials needed: 2 Iron Ore' / '1 Tin Ore, 2 Copper Ore' / '2 Iron Ore, 2 Coal, 1 Titanium Ore' — a perfect three-way match to the three branches. HELD. §1t401s0§.as:1058 is verbatim 'cost = §1t1525s0§.§1t9936s0§() * 10;' — the SAME node-level accessor used by the forge block at :1954, which I verified independently in the same file. :662 is verbatim 'this.detailstext.text = §1t1521s0§.getString(848,[_loc1_ * 10]);' and strings.json['848'] is 'Repair your currently equipped weapon?\nCost: [0] coins'. HELD, and the divergence warning is the valuable half. §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2296 reads verbatim 'internal static function §1t9590s0§(param1:int) : Number { if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5; }' — :2291, :2293 and :2295 match the quoted lines character for character. Its feeder §1t9589s0§ at :2279-2287 reads STAT_SPEED plus gear bonus ('§1t7356s0§(§1t9410s0§) + §1t7358s0§(§1t9410s0§)') and multiplies by 1.5 under a buff before calling it; :220 is 'internal static const §1t9410s0§:int = 8;' = STAT_SPEED. The android twin is named getSkillCooldownModifierVal (StatsManager.as:1854) and caps at 300 with '1 - speed / 300 * 0.5' at :1860 — so the divergence is real and I verified BOTH sides myself: v0.717 halves skill cooldowns at SPD 600, v0.682 at SPD 300. A recreation targeting the web build must take 600. RR:195 blocker (4) 'SPD->cooldown formula' closes as CONTRACT; RR:200 blocker (1) loses its cooldown half and keeps its DEF-mitigation half, exactly as the finding scopes it. Worth noting for whoever rewrites RR:200: its RANGE half also closes, via the dan/slash-length formula judged elsewhere in this packet.

REFUTED — not for being incomplete, but because two of the numbers it ships as the contract are FALSE, and one of them is the exact quantity the blocker asks for. (1) 'stance switch is free above 48 ... changing stance costs nothing' is wrong. The stance SETTER §1t3489s0§ (§1t99s0§.as:3083) contains, at :3160-3170, 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§()) { this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48; ... }' — a flat 48-Focus charge, clamped at 0, pushed to the HUD at :3169. The android twin de-obfuscates the guard: MCSPlayer.as:3096 'if(StageManager.isBattle())', :3098-3105 charging proportionally instead (reload > maxreload/2 -> maxreload/3, else -= maxreload/6). So switching stance IN BATTLE costs Focus in both builds, and the two builds even disagree on how much. RR:195 blocker (3) asks for 'max/fill/switch-cost'; the finding answers switch-cost with 'nothing', which would ship a wrong config constant. (2) 'regen +6/tick' is wrong. §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205 is the per-tick regen and it is '++this.§1t4414s0§' — plus ONE — pushed to the same HUD updater at :1208 (android MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160 identical). The +6 at :3320 is a KILL BONUS: its only caller is §1t1543s0§.as:2047-2049 'if(_loc4_ > 0) { ...§1t4479s0§(); }' where _loc4_ is the death count, and the android twin is literally named bonusReload, called from NPCManager.as:1709-1711 under 'if(deathCount > 0)'. (3) The claim 'that is the complete fill/consume/gate contract in one place' is false on its face — a third fill path exists, §1t120s0§.as:231 'param3.§1t4414s0§ = param3.§1t4415s0§ - 1;' (android SkillManager.as:218-219, case SKILL_FOCUS), which fills to max MINUS ONE, deliberately stopping short of the crit. What DOES hold: §1t1523s0§.as:2276 '48 + (SPD + gear) * 6' verbatim, the stance-weighted spend at :3302/:3306/:3310, and the full-bar zeroing at :3295-3297. I am re-filing those true parts under my own cites (FOCUS-FILL-CORRECTED, STANCE-SWITCH-COST-48) so nothing of value dies with the refutation, but the blocker does NOT close as this finding states it.

new_findings.text: The in-combat stance switch is neither free nor forbidden: it COSTS 48 Focus, flat, in web v0.717. The stance setter §1t3489s0§ (§1t99s0§.as:3083) ends with 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§()) { this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48; if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 0) { this.§1t4414s0§ = 0; } ... §1t5205s0§(reload, maxreload); }' at :3160-3170. The android twin names the guard — MCSPlayer.as:3096 'if(StageManager.isBattle())' — and charges a DIFFERENT price: :3098-3105 'if(this.reload > this.maxreload / 2) { this.reload = this.maxreload / 3; } else { this.reload -= this.maxreload / 6; }'. Combined with the entry gate at §1t99s0§.as:3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) { return; }', the v0.717 rule is: you may cycle stance in combat iff Focus >= 48, and doing so spends exactly 48. This closes the 'switch-cost' third of RR:195 blocker (3) with a number, and it is the second, independent kill on RR:158-160 — the ledger has the in-combat switch as removed 2014 behaviour and a recreation divergence, when it is in the target build's own source with a price tag.
new_findings.build: web v0.717 (android v0.682 charges proportionally instead — a real divergence)
new_findings.ledger_text: The *out-of-combat* switch costing Focus IS real; the *in-combat* switch is a recreation divergence — label it, don't present it as original.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core + L2 skills-meters. RR:159-160 is deleted, not softened; RR:195 blocker (3) gets its switch-cost: STANCE_SWITCH_FOCUS_COST = 48, gated on focus >= 48, charged only in battle.

new_findings.text: The Focus/reload FILL TRIGGER — the thing RR:190 blocker (5) asks a human to watch the bar for — is in source, and it is three paths, not one. (a) PASSIVE: §1t99s0§.as:1203-1208, inside the per-tick update right after §1t3270s0§(), 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§) { ++this.§1t4414s0§; ... §1t5205s0§(reload, maxreload); }' — plus ONE per tick, and it repaints the third HUD bar every tick. Android MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160 is identical. (b) ON KILL: the +6 at §1t99s0§.as:3320 is not a regen tick at all — its sole caller is §1t1543s0§.as:2047-2049 'if(_loc4_ > 0) { ...§1t4479s0§(); }' where _loc4_ is that pass's death count; the android twin is named bonusReload and is called from NPCManager.as:1709-1711 under 'if(deathCount > 0)'. So a kill (or a batch of them) is worth a flat +6. (c) SKILL: §1t120s0§.as:231 'param3.§1t4414s0§ = param3.§1t4415s0§ - 1;' (android SkillManager.as:218-219, 'case SKILL_FOCUS: owner.reload = owner.maxreload - 1;') — Replenish Focus fills the bar to maxreload MINUS ONE, i.e. it deliberately stops one point short of triggering the crit.
new_findings.build: both — web v0.717 primary, android v0.682 supplies the plain names
new_findings.ledger_text: ⑤ Focus/crit gating rule — *watch the Focus bar fill/consume.*
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core blocker (5) and the fill third of L2 skills-meters blocker (3) close as CONTRACT: FOCUS_REGEN_PER_TICK = 1, FOCUS_PER_KILL = 6, REPLENISH_FOCUS sets focus = maxFocus - 1. No Ruffle session needed, and no 'watch the bar' pass.

new_findings.text: RR:195 blocker (5) files the crit PROC rule as 'chance vs deterministic — entirely absent'. It is deterministic, and there is no dice roll anywhere near it. Web §1t99s0§.as:3272, inside the damage roll §1t4475s0§ (:3255), is 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' -> ':3274 return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;'. Those two members are reload and maxreload: the android twin getDamage (MCSPlayer.as:3198) has the same test in plain English at :3215 'if(this.reload == this.maxreload)'. Crit fires exactly when the Focus meter is FULL, every time, and §1t99s0§.as:3295-3297 zeroes the meter on the next swing, so a full bar buys exactly one crit. SEPARATE HAZARD, and it is a build-parity trap: the MULTIPLIER is web-only. Android MCSPlayer.as:3219 returns 'maxDamage * 1.2 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG' for non-Light stances and :3221 'maxDamage * 1.5 + ...' for Light. Anyone reading crit out of the android blobs gets 1.2/1.5, not 1.3 — and the wiki's 1.3 happens to match the WEB build only.
new_findings.build: web v0.717 (android v0.682 uses 1.2 / 1.5 — do not port)
new_findings.quote: §1t99s0§.as:3272 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' ‖ android MCSPlayer.as:3215 'if(this.reload == this.maxreload)' · :3219 'return maxDamage * 1.2 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG;' · :3221 'return maxDamage * 1.5 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG;'
new_findings.ledger_text: ⑤ crit **proc** rule (chance vs deterministic) — entirely absent.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters blocker (5) closes as CONTRACT: crit is deterministic on a full Focus meter, consumed by the swing that lands it. And CRIT_MULT = 1.3 must be labelled WEB v0.717 — an android-sourced port would ship 1.2/1.5.

new_findings.text: The dan-rank titles resolve completely, but not the way this packet's dan finding states. Both builds switch on STAT_DAN and render: dan 0 -> empty field; dan 1..9 -> getString(456)..getString(464). Web §1t5957s0§.as:3064-3102 and android InventoryUI.as:2274-2315 are the same switch, and grep for getString(455) returns ZERO hits across both decompiled trees — strings.json['455'] '(初段)' exists in the table but the game never displays it for a dan rank. So the display set is NINE titles: (弐段)(参段)(四段)(五段)(六段)(七段)(八段)(九段)(十段) over ten dan states 0-9, the cap being android StatsManager.as:2209 'if(getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) < 9)' -> :2211 'changeStat(STAT_DAN,1);'. There is also a SECOND, uncatalogued honorific layer the ledger has nowhere: the same switch appends a shogo title in #7D5500 to the character name — getString(465) 'Renshi' at dan 3-5, getString(466) 'Kyoshi' at dan 6-7, getString(467) 'Hanshi' at dan 8+.
new_findings.build: both — web v0.717 and android v0.682 carry the identical switch; title TEXT is read from the v0.682 table (S0-3 UI-copy caveat)
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 rebirth-elements blocker (3) at RR:205 closes: ten dan states, nine displayed titles at string ids 456-464, dan 0 blank, plus a Renshi/Kyoshi/Hanshi shogo overlay at 465/466/467. Also settles RR:164-165 by arithmetic — the '< 9' cap means MAX_DAN_RANK is 9 rebirths, not 10.

new_findings.text: Anyone porting the battle HUD from the android blobs will draw the third bar wrong. Web v0.717 normalises it at 48: §1t113s0§.as:328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);'. Android v0.682 normalises the SAME bar at 24: MCSPlayer.as:3272 'StageManager.getBattleUI().updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24));' and :1163-1168 'this.tempreload = this.reload - 24; ... updateReload(this.tempreload / (this.maxreload - 24));'. The AI's own low-Focus branch uses the same android constant — MCSPlayer.as:4528 'else if(this.reload < 24 && dice == 0)' against the web build's §1t4904s0§.as:632 'else if(§1t4414s0§ < 24 && _loc1_ == 0)', so 24 survives in one place on web too. Both builds compute the same capacity (48 + SPD*6: §1t1523s0§.as:2276 and android StatsManager.as:1841), so the divergence is purely in where the bar's zero point sits — and on web that zero point is the same 48 that gates the stance cycler.
new_findings.build: both — the divergence IS the finding
new_findings.lane_impact: L7 ui-hud: the third-bar fill formula must be labelled WEB v0.717 = (focus-48)/(maxFocus-48). It also means the empty-bar state (and therefore the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' label) covers focus <= 48 on web but focus <= 24 on mobile.
